stem: An infant is being assessed for possible central nervous system infection before urgent lumbar puncture; which finding is the strongest concern for raised intracranial pressure?
explanation: Bradycardia and hypertension are the strongest concern because they suggest raised intracranial pressure, which is important to recognise before lumbar puncture.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 136

optionExplanations.A: Correct because bradycardia with hypertension is a classic sign of raised intracranial pressure.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a recent upper respiratory tract infection does not by itself suggest raised intracranial pressure.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because immunisation history is background information rather than a sign of raised intracranial pressure.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because travel history may help identify infectious exposures but does not indicate raised intracranial pressure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because neck stiffness can suggest meningism, but it is not the strongest concern for raised intracranial pressure here.
